title: `mira-eva` renders black.

Airless render calibration
refs: **2026-07-22 slice landed:** Hapke `w` (single-scattering albedo) was pinned at 0.45 for every material while the caller applied albedo as a flat multiply, so mare and highland got *identical* multiple scattering (`H(mu0)H(mu)-1`) when it should collapse for dark material — the province contrast was only the linear albedo ratio, which tonemaps to near-invisible. `w` is now per-channel and material-driven (`hapke_w_from_albedo`, ×4.0 → highland 0.41 / mare 0.17 / fresh 0.94, matching the values this shader's own comment cites), the double albedo multiply is gone, and `HAPKE_OUTPUT_SCALE` restores the prior exposure so the change is contrast-only. Disc inspected: mare basin clearly separated, highland brightness held. `mira-orbit` unchanged (dominated by BL-33 speckle + flat 65° light). **Impostor blast radius checked 2026-07-22:** `shade_hapke_surface` is shared by `planet_impostor.wgsl` and `solid_planet.wgsl`, so every body impostor shades through it. Matched before/after `cloud-planet` captures (shader stashed for the baseline, same preset/world/seed) are visually indistinguishable — no blowout, colour shift, or terminator change; evidence in `artifacts/visual/runs/hapke_w_impostor/`. **Caveat:** that framing is cloud-dominated (clouds composite outside the Hapke path), so it is a weak test of the *land* path; a cloudless impostor framing would test it properly. Also removed the now-dead fixed-`w` `hapke_brdf` shim — nothing called it once `shade_hapke_surface` moved to the RGB entry point. **2026-07-22 second slice:** airless brightness lifted ~0.45 stop via `HAPKE_OUTPUT_SCALE` 0.128 → 0.175 (the one gain knob for the Hapke path; also reaches impostors, global exposure stays with GF-CAL), and inter-crater regolith smoothed — `AirlessRegolithParams` amplitude 50 → 15 m, base wavelength 700 → 1100 m. The old ±50 m over 700 m ran ~14% slopes with octaves to ~44 m and, being LOD-invariant, read as an all-over ripple at every range that competed with the craters; correcting the crater depth law (MIRA-V7) made that imbalance worse. Disc and approach both inspected: smooth between craters, craters read as bowls. Remaining V2 scope: opposition surge, terminator response. Refs: roadmap §"Visual targets" · gfx §3 · ADR-20260722T084155Z · `lighting.wgsl`

title: Crater ray systems
Single-face 4096 hero bake
Material/province node kind in the package schema
Airless crater speckle — FIXED (lighting normals; height aliasing ruled out by measurement)
refs: feature_compositor.rs · INC-0009 · mira-surface probe · **2026-07-22: reproduced far more severely by `mira-disc`/`mira-approach`/`mira-rim`; MIRA-V6 shows it blocks the close crater framing outright.** **Height-aliasing hypothesis FALSIFIED by measurement** — `terrain_baker diagnose` gained an alias audit (point sample at texel spacing vs box mean of the same span at 1 m). Baseline residual is only 0.148 m @ 25 m texel and 5.0 m @ 400 m against 107 m of within-texel relief, i.e. <5%: the height field is already effectively band-limited, because within-texel relief is dominated by the smooth slope across it and a midpoint sample of a ramp equals its mean. Three candidate fixes (footprint-faded crater compose; threshold-faded fBm octaves; sinc box-transfer fBm octaves) each made the residual 5–10× **worse** and were reverted. Search redirects to the **shading** path — normals/albedo — matching INC-0009, whose identical symptom class was also not geometry and was fixed shader-side. **ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-22 — it was the lighting normals, three compounding attenuations of resolved macro relief:** (1) `HEIGHT_NORMAL_WEIGHT` 0.35 applied only a third of the height atlas's normal; (2) `stable_normal` pulled another 15% back to the sphere; (3) `shade_hapke_surface` clamped n·l against **body curvature** plus a headroom that collapses to its 0.05 floor below `geo_n_dot_l` 0.15 — at 83° incidence that caps n·l near 0.17, so a crater wall tilted 30° sunward (true n·l ~0.60) shaded 3.5x too dark. Crater interiors could never exceed body-average brightness whatever their walls did: flat dark patches instead of bowls with a lit far wall, worst at grazing. These were blunt mitigations for INC-0009 that suppressed the signal rather than filtering it; its real fix (footprint-filtered octaves) has since landed. Now: weight 0.85, and `ThalosSurface` carries a separate `relief_normal_ws` so the micro-facet headroom references *resolved terrain* while `geo_normal_ws` stays sphere-outward for the grazing-view visibility floor — conflating the two blacked out the entire eye-level frame, which is exactly what the existing comment warned about. `mira-approach` verified: craters read as bowls with lit far walls
